A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-shattering study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original synthetic-Transformer experiments, knowledge-editing evaluations on pretrained models, and representation analyses, including Tables 1–4 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds causal-tracing and MLP key/value analyses in Appendix G.2.

M1.justification: The graph-generation procedure, two-layer Transformer, training objective, editing procedures, and shattering metric remain unchanged. The added assumption checks analyze the existing framework without modifying its method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic cyclic graphs, recall and inference tasks, calendar concepts, MMLU-Redux evaluation, and country/city experiments. Appendix G.2 adds diagnostics on the retained synthetic setup without expanding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, and PMET in the corresponding comparisons. The naturalistic experiments also retain their editing methods. Alternatives newly discussed in the conclusion are cited, not evaluated.

E3.justification: New Appendix G.2 introduces MLP-state restoration comparisons averaged over 100 randomly sampled prompts and PCA comparisons of keys and values for selected facts. Previously reported training settings, held-out evaluations, and sequential month-editing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.2 adds two focused assumption checks: causal tracing tests factual localization across the two MLP layers, and key/value visualizations examine the associative-memory interpretation. Existing cross-method, representation-location, counterfactual-distance, and naturalistic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing averaging and distribution reporting remain; the new 100-prompt diagnostic specifies a sample size without adding uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: New Figures 9–10 report stronger first-layer mediation and similar key/value patterns for facts sharing a target. V4 Figure 15 also adds previously unreported shattering annotations, including edit-row values 0.016, 0.027, 0.099, and 0.127. Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values and principal findings.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 corrects fact membership from the relation set R to the fact set F. Section 3.4 adds assertions about permutation sensitivity and what zero shattering implies. The metric formula and existing derivations remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and representation-shattering hypothesis remain. V4's conclusion additionally attributes editing fragility to entangled, compressed factual storage and suggests that mitigation may require reconsidering the localize-then-edit paradigm.

C2.justification: V4 adds a causal interpretation of the edit-distance manipulation while disclaiming formal proof, explains interference through parameter sharing and superposition, and expands the rationale for Isomap. Existing limitations concerning simplified models and naturalistic experiments remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the promise of a future code release with a specific repository location. New Appendix C documents inference prompts; Appendix B clarifies fact-level holdouts, and Section 4.5 explicitly describes ZeroEval's chain-of-thought use. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting associative memory, superposition, manifold analysis, retrieval augmentation, lifelong editing, and synthetic-document finetuning. These extend the discussion and research positioning, while the dedicated Related Work section remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 streamlines the abstract and several headings, rewrites the holdout explanation, expands explanatory passages, and adds an Impact Statement and appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from the preprint's single-column layout to a two-column conference layout. Figures and tables are extensively resized and repositioned; Figures 1 and 4 are rearranged or redrawn, and two new diagnostic figures are added.

improvement.justification: The new assumption checks, clearer prompts and holdout documentation, and concrete code-access instructions provide a limited net improvement in empirical support and reproducibility. The central results remain unchanged. A countervailing weakness is Section 3.4's new claim that zero shattering preserves entity locations: Equation 1 guarantees unchanged pairwise distances, not unchanged absolute positions.
